Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and colleagues on the Health and Human Services Committee, I am Representative Drew Gattine, and I am proud to serve House District 126, which includes portions of Saco,
Scarborough and Westbrook. I am pleased to appear before you to present LD 2154, An Act to Establish the
Health Information Technology Fund to Support a State-designated Statewide Health Information
Exchange.

This legislation seeks to create a platform for ongoing funding to safeguard Maine health care providers' access
to the information they require to safely treat patients, while unlocking a significant amount of federal funding at
a 3 :1 federal match rate. Beginning in fiscal year 2026-27, the bill creates and partially funds the Health
Information Teclmology Fund within the Department of Health and Human Services to support the operation
`
and sustainability of our state-designated statewide health information exchange, HealthInfoNet.

HealthInfoNet collects, stores and organizes confidential medical information and records for 2.2 million people. This information is available to providers so that care can be delivered safely and effectively. It connects providers and is relied upon by them, including hospitals, rural health centers and provider practices.
Government entities also rely on the data to ensure that care is being delivered in a high-quality manner, including MaineCare, Maine Centers for Disease Control, Maine Department of Corrections, and the Veterans Administration. Each day, approximately 9,000 providers utilize the compiled clinical data in the process of providing care to their patients in Maine.

In last year's budget the govemor proposed a new tax per bed tax on providers that use HealthlnfoNet in order to provide the funding to maintain the functionality of the system. Providers strongly objected to this new tax and we did not move forward with it in the budget. HealthInfoNet and providers, in particular Maine's hospitals, physicians and primary care clinics, went back to the drawing board and worked together to come up with the
proposal that I am presenting to you today.
I urge you to support LD 2154. This investment would maintain the quality and availability of HealthInfoNet
and help ensure Maine people receive the quality health care they deserve.

Thank you for your time and I am happy to answer questions.

To Whom It May Concern:
I am writing in strong support of LD 2154. I am a nurse serving vulnerable populations in a rural area of our state, and I have seen firsthand the critical value of having a statewide Health Information Exchange (HIE). For several years, the HIE has directly improved patient care, particularly for those who are medically or socially vulnerable.
The statewide HIE allows healthcare providers immediate access to real-time patient information, including comprehensive medical histories, recent imaging, laboratory results, consult reports, and notes from community-based care teams. This level of integration ensures that the care provided is informed, accurate, and consistent across all settings.
When a patient presents to the emergency department, the HIE gives the care team instant access to allergies, chronic conditions, advance directives, recent primary and specialty care visits, EMS reports, and patient-centered care plans. This information is especially critical for patients who are unable to communicate, cannot recall their medical history-- something very common during a medical emergency--or those who are elderly and medically complex.
I could share countless patient stories that demonstrate the impact of the HIE, but I will highlight two recent examples:
- A local self-employed carpenter without insurance came to our emergency department after his primary care provider ordered tests and imaging. Because the ER provider could view those results in real time through the HIE, additional testing was avoided. This saved the patient more than $1,500--an amount that would have created a significant financial barrier and likely discouraged him from seeking further care.
- An elderly patient arrived recently in a confused state and unable to communicate. Through the HIE, our team immediately accessed notes from her specialty oncology provider in Southern Maine. Without the HIE, we would not have known she was undergoing active cancer treatment or the specifics of her current regimen, which could have delayed or compromised her care. Instead, we were able to continue her treatment appropriately, view her medications, confirm her advance directives, and contact her family. Both the patient and her family expressed tremendous gratitude.
The Health Information Exchange is more than a repository of data--it tells the patient's story. It reflects their goals, identifies their care team and support system, and serves as a statewide, real-time personal health record accessible wherever they seek care in Maine. It improves safety, reduces unnecessary costs, and ensures that patient goals remain central to every care transition and clinical decision.

Thank you for your consideration of this important legislation.
Sincerely,
Jessica Taylor, MSN, BSN, RN, CCTM Senior Director, Population Health & Care Transitions St. Joseph Healthcare Bangor, Maine

Re: LD 2154 -- An Act to Establish the Health Information Technology Fund to Support a Statedesignated Statewide Health Information Exchange
Senator Ingwersen, Representative Meyer and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services:
Thank you for the opportunity to provide information neither for nor against LD 2154, An Act to Establish the Health Information Technology Fund to Support a State-designated Statewide Health Information Exchange.
This bill establishes a $1.8 million dollar Health Information Technology Fund within the Department of Health and Human Services to support the operation and sustainability of a state designated statewide Health Information Exchange (HIE) and to leverage the State's federal matching fund opportunity.
A statewide HIE is an essential component of Maine's health information infrastructure. The HIE strengthens Maine's healthcare system by linking individuals' clinical information from unaffiliated healthcare sites to create a single Electronic Health Record (EHR) that allows authorized providers across the state to better support and coordinate patient care. The Office of MaineCare Services (OMS) incentivizes and, in some cases, requires MaineCare provider participation and data sharing with the HIE through programs intended to improve health outcomes and reduce costs by improving coordination of care. DHHS also uses the aggregate information consolidated in the HIE to develop and advance population health efforts, care coordination programs, and delivery system reform initiatives.
When it comes to long-term funding options for the HIE, the Department has secured enhanced Federal Financial Participation (FFP) under an agreement with Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) known as an Operational Advanced Planning Document. Under this agreement, eligible state funding can draw down federal match at a rate of 25 percent state to 75 percent federal funds. To leverage this agreement fully, the state must have eligible state funds to draw down the federal dollars. The SFY 2024 supplemental budget, appropriated $1.7 million in general funds to maintain financial stability for the HIE through September 2025 using this federal approval. With the federal participation, this afforded a $6.8 million (all funds) investment. This bill's proposed state funding of $1.8 million, if all of it were eligible for FFP, would allow $7.2 million (all funds) of HIE operating costs to be covered through Medicaid,

annually. Of note, the current Cost Allocation Methodology (CAM) used to determine the allocation of operating expenses that may be funded by Medicaid is subject to change and contingent on ongoing CMS approval.
In an effort to establish a more sustainable funding source for the HIE that would leverage federal match and limit increases that health care providers have to shoulder with participant fees, the Department submitted a budget initiative last session to create a Health Information Technology Fund funded by an assessment on hospital inpatient services. The assessment would have replaced hospital participant fees, reducing hospital costs for HIE participation in the majority of cases. It could have been used for HIE operations, along with other Medicaid-related HIT projects that would be eligible for Medicaid FFP. This initiative was rejected. Since that time, the Department has been exploring options for securing state share and offers information on other alternatives to consider.
In the short term, the Department included funding to support the operations of the HIE within the proposed budget for the recently awarded Rural Health Transformation Program. This support is anticipated to be $1.25 million for Federal Fiscal Year 2026, subject to final CMS approval. In addition to this RHTP funding, the Department intends to maintain existing levels of contract for services HIN provides to the Department, totaling over $1 million in state and federal funds combined. There may also be the opportunity for future investment in new HIN initiatives that would be of benefit to the Department and the State of Maine.
The Department recommends using the federal resources from the RHTP grant rather than committing additional on-going general funds at this time. In the longer term, there are additional pathways to consider for the source of state share that may balance state general fund investment with other contributions. The Department is open to working with the sponsor and HIN on this bill to better meet these goals.
Please feel free to contact me if you have any questions during your deliberation of this bill.
Sincerely,
Michelle Probert Director Office of MaineCare Services Maine Department of Health and Human Services

Honorable Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services:
Community Care Partnership of Maine (CCPM) is pleased to support L.D. 2154, "An Act to Establish the Health Information Technology Fund to Support a Statedesignated Statewide Health Information Exchange (HIE)." CCPM is a clinically integrated network of 22 not-for-profit healthcare organizations across the state, including 17 federally qualified health centers and 5 community hospitals, and our members work collaboratively to advance population health in Maine--particularly in rural and underserved communities.
In furtherance of its mission to improve the health and well-being of communities across Maine, CCPM supports local care teams in delivering high-quality, cost-e ective, coordinated care. A secure and interoperable statewide Health Information Exchange is essential to that work. In rural Maine, where patients often travel long distances for care and receive services across multiple systems, an HIE is critical infrastructure that supports safer, more e icient, and more coordinated care.
As a condition of CCPM membership, we require participating organizations to connect to and use HealthInfoNet (HIN) bidirectionally, so information can both be accessed by care teams and contributed back to support continuity of care across settings. This expectation helps ensure that rural providers can reliably receive timely clinical information and that patient records are more complete statewide.
We also support our members in using HIN e ectively in day-to-day care management. CCPM routinely accesses HIN data and provides sta and care teams with daily, weekly, and monthly reports and actionable lists that help them prioritize outreach--such as patients who are currently admitted, recently discharged, or seen in the emergency department; patients with multiple recent ED visits; and patients flagged as higher risk for readmission based on recent utilization patterns and diagnoses. These reports help care teams focus scarce workforce resources on the patients most likely to benefit from timely follow-up, medication reconciliation, appointment scheduling, and connection to community supports.
A statewide HIE allows providers to access key clinical information in one place, including medication lists, lab and imaging results, diagnoses, discharge summaries, and emergency department visit information. This improves care coordination and patient safety, especially for older adults with complex conditions, people with substance use disorders, and veterans who receive care in both VA and non-VA settings. When rural providers can see recent hospitalizations, medication changes, and test results in real time, they can avoid duplicative testing, reduce preventable readmissions, and manage chronic disease closer to home.

Beyond individual patient care, CCPM uses HIN data to gain insights and analytics across our member network--particularly around potentially avoidable emergency department utilization. By examining patterns such as frequent ED use, repeat visits for ambulatory-care-sensitive conditions, and variations by geography or clinic service area, CCPM and our members can identify where targeted resourcing and interventions will have the greatest impact. These insights directly inform outreach and education e orts for patients, care management workflows, after-hours access strategies, and partnership decisions with EMS and community-based organizations.
Maine has already demonstrated leadership through its state-designated statewide HIE, including broad participation from rural providers and bi-directional connectivity with VA facilities. These connections also support public health reporting and emerging "community information exchange" e orts that better link clinical care with social services. However, maintaining and expanding this statewide capability requires predictable, long-term funding--particularly as earlier federal HITECH-era funding has ended and as cybersecurity and resilience needs continue to grow.
L.D. 2154 is a critical step toward long-term sustainability by establishing a Health Information Technology Fund to support Maine's state-designated statewide HIE. This investment would help sustain core HIE services that rural organizations depend on; strengthen cybersecurity and technical resilience that small facilities cannot a ord to build alone; and expand connections to essential partners in the rural care continuum.
With stable funding in place, the statewide HIE can continue to support safe, e icient, coordinated care across Maine--particularly for rural communities that cannot a ord fragmented information systems or uneven access to essential clinical data.
CCPM respectfully urges the Committee to support L.D. 2154.
Respectfully submitted,
Sandy Nesin, Esq. Chief Executive O icer Community Care Partnership of Maine

Good morning, Chairs Senator Ingwersen & Representative Meyer, and honorable members of the Joint Standing Committee on Health and Human Services. My name is Shaun Alfreds and I am the Executive Director and CEO of HealthlnfoNet, the operator of the state designated statewide health information
exchange referred to as the HIE.
I am pleased to be before you today to testify in strong support for LD 2154, an Act to Establish the
Health Information Technology Fund to Support a State--designated Statewide Health Information Exchange (HIE).
Background HealthlnfoNet is an independent, 501(c)3 nonprofit organization that has operated the HIE in Maine since 2006. Maine's HIE links an individual's health information from unaffiliated healthcare providers to
create a single statewide patient electronic health record improving the coordination of the patient's care which leads to better health outcomes.
Maine's statewide HIE is governed by 22 MRSA �1711-C, among other state and federal laws, and is
recognized as a national leader in helping to create system-wide improvements in patient care and population health. It currently brings together vital health information from all the state's acute hospitals, federally qualified health centers, most outpatient locations and post-acute and long-term care facilities, behavioral health centers, social service agencies, community-based organizations, as well as MaineCare, the Maine Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Maine CDC), the Maine
Department of Corrections, the Veterans Administration (VA), among other sources. Currently, the HIE contains health records for more than 2.2 million Individuals (both in-state and out-of-state residents), which are made available to healthcare clinicians and staff to help improve the safety, quality, and
delivery of care they provide to Maine people. Today, over 9,000 clinicians across the state log into the HIE to access over 250,000 Maine residents' medical records every month. Maine's HIE provides a comprehensive suite of services that enables providers statewide to support data-informed health care coordination and management.
Recognizing this, the Maine Department of Health and Human Services (Maine DHHS) applied for and
was awarded federal funding through the U.S. Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) to
sustain the operations of Maine's HIE.

CMS awarded these funds based on evidence that improved access to patient data, and the HiE's
management of the data have supported better outcomes and reduced costs across Medicaid, Medicare, and a range of pubiic health programs.
The CMS funding conditions, which is a 3:1 federal/state financial contribution, requires the state to provide a match. CMS directed that the match must come from the state itself, not from HealthlnfoNet
or the provider community. For FY 2025, the legislature approved $1.7IVI in funding from the
Supplemental Budget while the State and HealthlnfoNet worked to develop a sustainable way to fund the annual match for FY 2026/2027. The Department of Human services put forward a hospital bed tax for FY 2026 that was not approved by the Joint Standing Committee on Appropriations and Financial Affairs due to concerns about inclusivity of all stakeholders and philosophical concerns about the tax
implementation.
After the proposed hospital bed tax was not approved in 2025, the provider community, HIN, and Maine stakeholders came together and agreed to work with the Legislature on this direct funding
approach.
LD 2154 is focused solely on creating a health information technology fund for the state-designated statewide HIE. The fund, to be seeded by a direct appropriation is to only be used for the state-match to
draw down the 3:1 federal money that would then support the long-term operations of the HIE. By doing so, all Maine providers would no longer have to pay for access to the statewide HIE that has become so critical for them to deliver high quality care and improve patient safety. In all, this will save the provider community over $4.3M annually. Moreover, this investment by the state would reduce the barrier to the small "last mile" health care practices from joining the HIE, thereby improving what is already a widely coveted and used system. As you all know on this committee, to deliver goodcare, our clinical providers need the most current and comprehensive information on their patients -- the HIE delivers that.
What Happens if the Legislature Does Not Establish the HIT Fund for State Match This
Session?
Unprecedented financial pressures on the health care delivery system have forced many providers in our State to reduce needed services just to "keep the lights on" . By supporting the 3:1 federal match,
HealthlnfoNet can directly and immediately reduce the financial burden on struggling providers while continuing to provide clinicians across our state vital information they need to provide care. Without this state match, HealthlnfoNet would need continue to increase subscription fees on the already overburdened provider community, potentially putting them in a position of withdrawing from the HIE. This would undermine not only the goals of health reform but also the value of the HIE directly impacting patient care and safety.
Thank you for the opportunity to provide testimony in support of the Hi'l' Fund. On behalf of HealthinfoNet and the many organizations that rely on the HIE, we respectfuliy urge your support for
this initiative.
